title: Classic '80s board game HeroQuest gets a PC port
content:
The classic '80s dungeon crawler board gameHeroQuest is getting its first official digital release, with a PC version coming to Steam some time in 2027. The game is being made by digital board game devs Nomad Games, best known for the video game adaptations of Talisman, as well as a couple of Fighting Fantasy titles. They know their old games, this lot!

The title will feature the four classic HeroQuest characters of the Elf, Barbarian, Dwarf, and Wizard, who'll combine their powers to defeat the evil sorcerer Zargon. It will have online co-op, so you can play the game controlling all the heroes, or just one. Just like the original, you can also take control of the dungeon as Zargon, and plot the characters' untimely doom.

HeroQuest is an extremely lightweight (in rules, not components) dungeon crawler RPG board game published by Milton Bradley and Games Workshop in 1989.

After Hasbro acquired the license at the start of the decade, its board game maker subsidiary Avalon Hill relaunched HeroQuest in 2022. By 2023, it had remade most of the original adventures and began to craft its own, keeping up a steady stream of new content, most recently the Wizards of Morcar quest pack in 2026.

I have my fingers crossed some of this extra content will quickly make its way into this digital edition (hopefully in the base game) as the original HeroQuest gameplay, while certainly nostalgic for anyone who enjoyed it the first time around, is rather simplistic.

It's still early days, and we don't have price information or a more exact release window to share just yet, but stay tuned for this in 2027.

Honestly, I'm surprised there wasn't already a digital version of HeroQuest - it seems like such a no-brainer. Then again, I suppose in the transition to screens you do lose some of that glorious tactility of the physical version. After all, the best thing about HeroQuest is the minis!

If you love tabletop games, you'll probably enjoy our Discord - the best place to enjoy all the latest news with likeminded folk.

title: Trench Crusade Warband Focus: The Drowned Choir
content:
Welcome everyone to a Heretical Warband Focus on Tabletop Battles. We are diving headfirst into the moshpit that is The Drowned Choir. Prepare for the battle onstage as these Choristers gaslight and gatekeep their way to stardom. 

The Lore

A plague that wreaks havoc alongside the coast, consuming each hamlet and fishing village that dots the region along the waterways. It is not a war fought outright, but a battle within the minds and will of the denizens. As they are ground down and worn thin by the torments of the night, until the voices draw them closer to the deep blue enveloping tides. Jealousy and Envy bathe themselves upon them all, a bloodthirsty call drags them to the brink. All will join the deep enveloped by Leviathan; all will join the Choir of the Drowned.

The Variant

Before we dive in, lets get our feet wet with the variants rules:

  • A Song Within the Deep: Our band gets to rock it out with 3 vocalists, aka 3 Drowned Choristers. On top of this we get a star performer by upgrading one of our Drowned Choristers into a Leviathal Chorus. This gives our headliner TOUGH and LEADER Keywords alongside a base size bump to 40mm for a measly 20 ducats. Our Leviathal Chorus also upgrades their aura ability:

    • Dread Harmony: Our headliner profits from that further by causing all rolls in their aura to become Risky. With 2 of our 3 choristers applying the negative dice auras (it should be noted these don't stack) these two auras combine for some nasty debuffs.
  • A Wretched Chorus: Every band needs some useful groupies. Our wretched cost 5 ducats more but it's worth every coin. They go to a Melee Characteristic of +0 DICE and gain +1 to Melee while within 8” of a Drowned Chorister/Leviathal Chorus. Give these guys double clubs and you got 36 ducat lads that can punch better than most other chaff units in the game.
  • Mounting Madness: What’s better than an 8” aura farming chorister? A 12” aura farming chorister of course! When any Drowned Chorister’s or Leviathal Chorus is within 8” of one another, they bump their radius by 4”. This allows some wild board coverage and application of their Auras. Your opponent's are going to have a hard time avoiding your auras when they cover half the table.
  • To No Purpose Save Their Own: There are no other elites you can take in this warband. Additionally, we lose access to the Sea Hag (Artillery Witch for you landlubbers) and Anointed.

This variant is spelled out in two words “Aura Farming”. We are manipulating dice rolls and trying to trip up the opponent as much as possible and rush screaming wretched at them to pin them in place. We lose a lot within this variant, and have really no meaningful platforms to carry our long range weapons. This means we'll be focusing on a melee build.

Unique Battlekit

Credit: Brandon (Zaros) Oelfke

While we have no unique battlekit, it is worth mentioning 2 pieces that stand out as astoundingly beneficial and useful within our variant.

Diving Bell - 10 Ducats

No rolls for climbing or jumping and no injury rolls for falling is an amazing addition for only 10 ducats. This lets our Choristers move throughout the map and position in a way that is a nuisance for the enemy to respond to while we aura farm and apply our debilitating debuffs. It also means we can Diving Charge people with no potential harm to ourselves, which leads to some fun scenarios.

Wreckers Torch - 15 Ducats

There's a concept I used when I was playing a lot of heretic legion; the Budget Chorister. 97 ducats for standard, Shield, & Polearm lets them be the cheap aura annoyance they are and slot into a starting warband list easily. The Wreckers Torch is an upgrade to Polearm for only 8 ducats, and we are happy to pay up. The Fire keyword is an astounding addition alongside armor piercing. This will let us hold weight while still being a budget. 

The Units

Leviathal Chorus

Credit: Brandon (Zaros) Oelfke

Our star performer with their TOUGH and LEADER keyword is ready to take the stage! They are a key model to our game plan; get our opponent to fail rolls and end their activation early. We do not have a lot of punch in the list, we'll win the war of attrition by slowing the opponent down and playing the objective. The main thing to remember, is that EVERY roll becomes risky, including any mission specific actions that have rolls models need to make. We can penalize and make the opponent make mission rolls at negative dice with risky to ensure we are outscoring them.

Choristers famously hate guns, but if you can get strong on them the Heavy Flamethrower will work wonders. With these 3 models being the linchpin in our strategy, it is important to armor up as much as possible. We can push to -3 with reinforced and shield easily, although standard armor and shield works early on.

The BLOCK keyword early is a great addition on all our Choristers for cheap survivability vs melee warbands. By combining the Drowned Chorister’s Aura, FEAR Keyword, and BLOCK Keyword we bring them to -3 Dice to hit. Most Leaders are only +2, meaning we can even drop them into the negatives. Combined with the aforementioned -3 armour, and we have some really tanky models.

Loadout Considerations:

  • Wrecker’s Torch + Shield (Early)
  • Double Sac Blades (Later)
  • Heavy Flamethrower (If STRONG gained)

Wretched

Credit: Brandon (Zaros) Oelfke

Our fanboys cost a bit more but the utility they give within this variant is phenomenal. Our 3 choristers are our lynchpin, losing one early is a problem and can spell the end of our gameplan. These guys are here to muck up the opponent and prevent them from getting to our choristers while we play the mission. With their bonuses to melee, they aren’t ignorable either.

The best part is they are still wretched! Meaning, when they die we get to give our choristers a blessing marker which will help make them more survivable. This works both ways though, since they punch more reliably, they may take out an Elite and earn their freedom.

Loadout Considerations:

  • Double Clubs (No reason for swords at +1/0 Dice)
  • Sharktooth Talisman (Spicy addition in late game campaigns for even more reliable beaters)
  • Shotgun (Same as Talisman, we value double clubs so we can charge in and gum up movement more, but when we have money to throw around this is an option)

The List

One Trench Direction - Campaign Starter

Faction: The Drowned Choir

Rating: 700 Ducats | 0 Glory

Patron: None

## Elites ##

Leviathal Chorus Chorister - 135D

Upgrades & Choices: Leviathan Bell

Battlekit: Wrecker's Torch, Standard Armour, Trench Shield

Drowned Chorister - 115D

Upgrades & Choices: Leviathan Bell

Battlekit: Wrecker's Torch, Standard Armour, Trench Shield

Drowned Chorister - 115D

Upgrades & Choices: Leviathan Bell

Battlekit: Wrecker's Torch, Standard Armour, Trench Shield

## Troops ##

Heretic Raider - 70D

Upgrades & Choices: Infiltrator

Battlekit: Flamethrower

Heretic Raider - 70D

Upgrades & Choices: Infiltrator

Battlekit: Flamethrower

Heretic Raider - 51D

Battlekit: Pistol, Musical Instrument

Choir Wretched - 36D

Battlekit: Trench Club, Trench Club

Choir Wretched - 36D

Battlekit: Trench Club, Trench Club

Choir Wretched - 36D

Battlekit: Trench Club, Trench Club

Choir Wretched - 36D

Battlekit: Trench Club, Trench Club

This list is my main list I utilize for running Drowned Choir. It allows us to start a campaign with all three Choristers, anti armor in the means of two infiltrating flamethrowers, a musician to guarantee movement with four dice dashes, and our crew of Wretched. We save money by being standard + shield for all three Choristers alongside the phenomenal Wrecker's Torch. Our immediate game two upgrade is reinforced armor to our Leader alongside another body, then game three we slam double sac knives on our Leader to let them be the beyblade they were born to be. Stay at max threshold count as much as possible through Troopers/Legionnaires and Wretched, fishing to turn elite Legionnaires into heavy weapon platforms in the campaign!

Final Thoughts

I'm generally a big Horde faction fan. This takes that concept and twists it on its head. It is a horde faction that isn’t designed to be a murder machine. Wretched punch better, but are still wet noodles that lose to fear and we have to treat our choristers like glass so we don’t lose our lynchpins. The Drowned Choir aims to manipulate the rolls and control the match through positioning and body blocking which makes it truly unique. Your friends are gonna love hearing you remind them before they roll that it is “-1 Dice and Risky”.

title: Tabletop Battles Reviews: BRAZILIAN DRUG DEALER BEFORE 4
content:
I am going to start this review off with a very important caveat: I am not Brazilian.

But by the grace of God, I am a fan of boomer shooters, and the BRAZILIAN DRUG DEALER series (the caps are important) is one of the best boomer shooter series on the market. Although this review is specifically about 4, the entire series spans 2 games that are available on itch.io, and 3 and 4, which are currently on Steam. When I was offered the chance to review 4, I really had very little idea of what I was getting into, and within 5 minutes of playing 4, I stopped and immediately went to get the other 3 games to properly enjoy the newest one.

What I experienced is a game that is a love letter on multiple levels: to genre, to games, to music, and to Brazilian culture. There are certainly other Boomer Shooters you can buy and play, but none of them are going to give you the pure unadulterated joy that BRAZILIAN DRUG DEALER BEFORE 4: DEMONS FROM THE PORTAL TO HELL I OPENED ARE STILL IN THE FAVELA AND NOW I HAVE TO SAVE MAMADAS FROM RONALDO will.

A code for BRAZILIAN DRUG DEALER BEFORE 4 was provided by the publisher; however, I purchased 1-3 on my own. 

BRAZILIAN DRUG DEALER BEFORE 4 opens with almost inscrutable text on a loud, garish background that immediately asks you if you want to learn about new movement tech. Good news: being Brazilian has gifted you with the ability to double jump, and also you can air dash. The movement and speed of BRAZILIAN DRUG DEALER BEFORE 4 are key to understanding just why this game is so much fun: it doesn't have sliding or parkour in the sense that more modernized game engines might allow, but the sheer mobility you have in this game approaches levels that maybe only ULTRAKILL pulls off as well. The jumps and dashes are responsive, and the kinetic energy in the game sucked me in to the point that I turned down multiple invitations to play my current mainstay game, Deadlock, to instead sink 6 hours into playing this series. Sorry friends, now you know why I kept dodging you.

One of my favorite memories from college was sitting in my dorm room playing Serious Sam while my roommate blasted Ludacris on a particularly cool Fall day. We received a noise complaint that we ignored and ordered pizza that probably tasted terrible, and we capped the day off by blowing off our Astronomy course that we both later had to withdraw from because we missed an exam on that exact day that was worth 20% of our grade. I use this memory lightly because it is one of the pinnacles of gaming memories and joy for me, and BRAZILIAN DRUG DEALER BEFORE 4: DEMONS FROM THE PORTAL TO HELL I OPENED ARE STILL IN THE FAVELA AND NOW I HAVE TO SAVE MAMADAS FROM RONALDO is the closest I have felt to that memory in over 20 years. To veer into gaming review terminology for a few moments, the game has tight controls, fast gameplay, a sense of speed and style, and energetic music that helps push you to continue playing. To stop sounding like people trying to avoid using the word "fun", this game is pure, unadulterated fun that costs less than 10 dollars.

I like Boomer Shooters, probably too much. My first PC gaming experience was Wolfenstein 3D, and I remember being so excited that my mom let me play Duke Nukem 3D; it was even my first online gaming experience, which was some of the most jank garbage ever.  BRAZILIAN DRUG DEALER BEFORE 4 does, to the point that it makes me feel a similar electricity to playing Ultrakill for the first time did, which is something that all good Boomer Shooters do: they remind me of what it was like to beat Doom II, Wolfenstein, Duke Nukem, and all the rest. The game is garish, EXCEPTIONALLY loud, and both feels great to shoot and move in. The music is bumping and frenetic, and everything is so Brazilian that even barely understanding any of the jokes, references, or touches somehow wraps around to making perfect sense. Perhaps it also just works because BRAZILIAN DRUG DEALER BEFORE 4 is not trying to sell me on cinematic realism, narrative, or high fidelity graphics, but instead on the base principles of what a Boomer Shooter is, what Quake is, and then handing me dual drink bottles to shoot people with and saying have fun with a wink.

I played on the hardest difficulty for the review, and I found that the game was a solid challenge but still a bit of a breeze if you're comfortable with these types of games; that isn't to say it was easy, and the autosave feature might be one of the best things the game offers because it makes retrying areas smooth; I died a lot. Like, a lot a lot, but it never felt particularly frustrating when I did so; I remember playing through a lot of the modern Doom games feeling occasional moments of annoyance at how the fights were designed, but also the fact that dying would often create a pretty unsatisfying loop of downtime. Not here; death here is just about as simple as hitting Y and trying it again, which I was more than happy to do. After I finished my playthrough, I gave the other difficulties a shot to see what the game would be like at various levels, and although I do think the easier ones are a little too easy, I do appreciate that they still resulted in the sense of speed and energy the game wanted to present. I mentioned that I enjoy Boomer Shooters, and something that I think it often misunderstood with modern titles is that "harder" means the game should be exceptionally punishing or even tiring, turning enemies into bullet sponges and battles into grueling endurance fights, while making easy difficulties almost walking simulators. When I was younger, I played on easier difficulties and often used cheat codes because the games were just hard, even on lower difficulties, which meant that they were tuned better to what type of experience level I was expected to have going in; as a kid who had never played a shooter at all in my life, the easier Wolfenstein difficulties were still hard, and I feel that if you are not that familiar or comfortable with Boomer Shooters but want to try them, BRAZILIAN DRUG DEALER BEFORE 4 makes sure players can experience what the game is doing without punishing them by giving them an extremely reduced version of the "real" game, nor does it force them to play at a difficulty they won't enjoy.

I will say I didn't get to do much with the multiplayer; there are options to play cooperatively and also deathmatch, and I did try deathmatch a few times which was fun, but it wasn't something I've spent a lot of time with in my time with BRAZILIAN DRUG DEALER BEFORE 4; I might give it another shot, but for me, the real joy is running, jumping, and gunning through the main campaign. Of course, as the game is less than 10 dollars, the fact that it even has a functional and fun multiplayer at all is magical, really. There is also a rocket jump feature and the game encourages you to replay it, particularly with rocket jumping and otherwise, to pursue specific secrets and challenges; like most older Boomer Shooters, some of the puzzles are obtuse and fairly opaque, really asking players to think a little outside of what is being asked to solve them, but I didn't find myself struggling forever on them, which was something I appreciated; hunting for the single hidden pixel that signals a secret or similar other things I've done in other games is one of the things I like the least in Boomer Shooters, because they break the speed and sense of kinetic energy that the games thrive on.

Perhaps my only regret with the game is that I just don't know enough about Brazilian culture to understand the jokes and references that are present; I recognize some things and people I've picked up through osmosis from having Brazilian friends, but there is a lot going on here and sometimes it is going on so fast that perhaps being familiar with it wouldn't help anyway. This isn't a knock against the game, though, but more a knock against the human experience; I can't know or understand everything, and it is frustrating! But what I can recognize is that this is a game made by people that love their cultural identity, rather than one that is mocking and stereotyping it. And that sense of love, even taken to comedic extremes and absurd weapons like bottles of guarana drink, a sandal, or a shower, feels fun.

I love this game. I think that part is very obvious, but I want to state that the other 3 games are equally as good, and I really do suggest giving them a shot and playing through the series before you get to 4. If you really don't care and just want to know what the hell I'm talking about when I say that double jumping and air dashing because you shoved fireworks up your ass feels great while you shoot enemies with two bottles of Guarana Golly that work like automatic pistols before collecting a key that opens a giant black texture that reads ENTER HERE, then just start with 4 on Steam and have an amazing time for a few hours. I think the game absolutely sings as a single playthrough experience, so clear a few hours for yourself, put on some headphones (or torture those around you) and consider taking a trip to Brazil.

Have any questions or feedback? Drop us a note in the comments below or email us at contact@tabletopbattles.com. Want articles like this linked in your inbox every Monday morning? Sign up for our newsletter. And don't forget that you can support us on Patreon for backer rewards like early video content, Administratum access, an ad-free experience on our website, and subscriber-only content covering competitive Warhammer 40K!

title: All Legendary Pokémon and Mythical Pokémon in order
content:
Legendary Pokémon are iconic - they have the most elaborate designs, the best stats, and some of the mightiest Pokémon cards. While all Mythical and Legendary Pokémon were once few in number, each new game has added more. To help you keep track, we've created this handy list of all 71 Legendaries and 23 Mythicals you can catch or collect.

If you'd like a complete Legendary and Mythical Pokémon list, this guide can provide - but our full 'How many Pokémon are there?' guide covers pocket monsters of all kinds. If you like rare and powerful things, you might also be interested in our guides to rare Pokémon cards and the best Pokémon cards. For now, though, let's meet the legends.

  • Gen 1
  • Gen 2
  • Gen 3
  • Gen 4
  • Gen 5
  • Gen 6
  • Gen 7
  • Gen 8
  • Gen 9
  • Gen 10
  • FAQ

Gen 1 Legendary Pokémon

NameImagePokédex #TypeBase Stat Total
Articuno#144Ice/Flying485
Zapdos#145Electric/Flying490
Moltres#146Fire/Flying495
Mewtwo#150Psychic590

In Pokémon Red and Blue, Mewtwo was an end-game secret. It appears in the high-level Cerulean Cave, which can only be accessed after beating the Elite Four and winning the Pokémon League.

In the English language version of Pokèmon, Articuno, Zapdos, and Moltres have names that end in the Spanish words for one, two, and three. Their Japanese names are a lot more descriptive: フリーザー (Furiizaa), aka Freezer; サンダー (Sandaa), aka Thunder; and ファイヤー(Faiyaa), aka Fire.

Gen 1 Mythical Pokémon

 NameImagePokédex #TypeBase Stat Total
Mew#151Psychic500

Mew was never intended to be a publicly available Pokémon. Developer Shigeki Morimoto added Mew to the code as an Easter egg just for his colleagues at Game Freak, using space on the cartridge that was freed up after debug tools were removed. Some players discovered Mew via glitches, starting rumors of a secret Pokémon that were hard for fans to verify or disprove in the early days of the internet.

The first time players could legitimately catch Mew was in Spring 1996, when Game Freak ran a promotion in manga magazine CoroCoro Comic, offering a few lucky winners the chance to mail in their game cartridge to have Mew added to their Pokédex.

How rare is Mew?

In the world of Pokémon, there is only one Mew. According to the events of Pokémon: The First Movie, Mew is an ancient species of Pokémon long thought extinct.

Mew is generally only available during special events. For example, in September 2023, it was possible to use a Mystery Gift and a code to unlock Mew in Pokemon Scarlet and Violet - but that code has since expired. However, it is available in Pokémon Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl if you have save data from Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! or Let's Go: Eevee! on your Switch.

Gen 2 Legendary Pokémon

NameImagePokédex #TypeBase Stat Total
Raikou#243Electric580
Entei#244Fire580
Suicune#245Water580
Lugia#249Psychic/Flying680
Ho-Oh#250Fire/Flying680

Four-legged counterparts to the Legendary birds, Raikou, Entei, and Suicune were the games' first 'roaming Pokémon'. Instead of appearing as static encounters, they could be found out in the world.

Ho-Oh was the 152nd Pokémon ever revealed, and the first sign that The Pokémon Company planned to expand beyond the original 151.

Not only was Ho-Oh teased in the CoroCoro magazine, but it also made an appearance in the very first episode of the Pokémon anime. Protagonist Ash Ketchum spots a Ho-Oh, but his Pokédex is unable to identify it.

Lugia is a lead character in the second Pokémon movie 'The Power of One', the leader of the Legendary birds, and the only one who is able to stop their squabbling.

Gen 2 Mythical Pokémon

NameImagePokédex #TypeBase Stat Total
Celebi#251Psychic/Grass600

When the time came for the Pokémon Company to make follow-ups to its unexpected global smash hit game, it had a much better idea of what kinds of things would be popular with fans - and it was determined to repeat the success of the mythical Mew. Enter Celebi, which, unlike its forebear, was planned for in advance.

Which isn't to say it was much easier to get Celebi, at least not in the original release. The critter would only spawn if the player acquired a Great Smith's Ball. Not only was this item only available during a special event, you needed to use the rudimentary cell data transfer from the Game Boy Color's 'Game Boy Mobile' peripheral - something that was only available for the Japanese version of the handheld!

Did you know? Sprites from a datamined beta version of Gold and Silver seem to show this Pokémon originally started out as something closely resembling a depiction of Kokopelli, a Native American fertility deity. It ended up being worked into a very different kind of creature, although Celebi still makes the plants grow.

Gen 3 Legendary Pokémon

NameImagePokédex #TypeBase Stat Total
Regirock#377Rock580
Regice#378Ice580
Registeel#379Steel580
Latias#380Dragon/Psychic600
Latios#381Dragon/Psychic600
Kyogre#382Water670
Groudon#383Ground670
Rayquaza#384Dragon/Flying680

Rayquaza has the highest base Attack, Special Attack, and the highest total of all base stats, of any Dragon-type or Flying-type Pokémon - but it has sometimes been very easy to catch.

In Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire, Rayquaza was needed to progress the Delta Episode side plot. The developers changed its catch rate from 3 to 45 (higher means easier, so this was a huge change) to ensure players would be able to snatch up the big green noodle. This was reverted in Scarlet and Violet when the mighty dragon reappeared in The Hidden Treasure of Area Zero.

Regice, Regirock, and Registeel, also called the Giants of Legend, are some of the trickiest Legendary Pokémon to find in the games. In Ruby, Sapphire, or Emerald, you have to translate braille and then do a bunch of puzzles to unlock them.

Latios and Latias are, effectively, the same species, with Latios being male and Latias being female - just like the male and female Nidoran evolutionary line.

Kyogre is one of many Legendary Pokémon we're labeling as a 'potential apocalypse'. It has the ability to control the level of the oceans, and is believed by some to be the creator of the oceans in primordial times. In Pokémon Sapphire and Emerald, team Aqua has the very normal goal of finding Kyogre and using it to raise the sea levels to create more homes for aquatic Pokémon (never mind how many countries get flooded in the process!).

Groudon and Kyogre famously don't get on, as the former is said to have fallen into a long slumber after an apocalyptic battle with the latter. Perhaps it's because Groudon is, in myth, considered to be responsible for creating continents. Land and sea are just too different, it seems.

Gen 3 Mythical Pokémon

NameImagePokédex #TypeBase Stat Total
Jirachi#385Steel/Psychic600
Deoxys#386Psychic600

Jirachi is a bit like a mythical genie, a Pokémon that sleeps for a thousand years at a time before waking up to grant three wishes. While all the anime stories about Jirachi centre on this wish-granting ability - and what happens when people abuse it - in game, it stands out for a very different reason. It's the only Pokémon capable of learning the move Doom Desire, a damage dealing Steel type move.

Is Deoxys even a Pokémon, when it evolved from an extra-terrestrial virus? It's in the Pokédex, so we guess it still counts. This strange Pokémon does not evolve, but it can change between four Formes by being exposed to different meteorites: Normal Forme, Attack Forme, Defense Forme, and Speed Forme. And it has another ability that has never appeared in a game: in the comics it's capable of creating clones of itself!

Gen 4 Legendary Pokémon

NameImagePokédex #TypeBase Stat Total
Uxie#480Psychic580
Mesprit#481Psychic580
Azelf#482Psychic580
Dialga#483Steel/Dragon680
Palkia#484Water/Dragon680
Heatran#485Fire/Steel600
Regigigas#486Normal670
Giratina#487Ghost/Dragon680
Cresselia#488Psychic600

The Legendary Pokémon that appeared in Pokémon Diamond and Pearl really push the power level for the franchise. Dialga has the ability to control time, Palkia can warp space, and together they are capable of creating new universes.

Meanwhile, Giratina can rip holes in reality and lurks in the Distortion dimension. Many fans think of him as Pokémon's equivalent of the devil.

Uxie, Mesprit, and Azelf are the three Lake Guardians of the Sinnoh region. Their Pokédex entries reveal they are associated with knowledge, emotion, and willpower respectively. This is a reference to the 'three sacred treasures' of Japan, artifacts that belong to the Imperial Japanese household and can be traced back to ancient myth - a mirror that represents wisdom, a jewel that represents benevolence, and a sword that represents valor.

Heatran is believed to be the physical embodiment of the planet's core. It would apparently go on a magma-fueled rampage if a Magma Stone didn't keep it sealed in a volcanic crater. So, you know, it's the perfect companion for a 10-year-old Pokémon trainer.

Cresselia has slightly more chill. This ethereal lunar Pokémon specializes in healing, and its feathers even give someone who holds it pleasant dreams.

On both ends of the 'chill vs not chill' scale is Regigigas, a Pokémon with far too many Gs in its name. This legendary is credited with creating a legion of other legendary giants. While it can be calm and thoughtful, Regigigas can also cause immense devastation when rampaging - and has the power to override the authority of any puny human who might think they control one of Regigigas' creations.

Gen 4 Mythical Pokémon

NameImagePokédex #TypeBase Stat Total
Phione#489Water480
Manaphy#490Water600
Darkrai#491Dark600
Shaymin#492Grass600
Arceus#493Normal720

Arceus is perhaps the most powerful Mythical Pokémon. It's worshiped as a deity by some humans, who may actually be right - it could be the creator of the Pokémon universe.

On the less powerful side is Darkrai, who is apparently harmless but likes to keep people away by inflicting them with horrific nightmares. These can be stopped with a feather from Darkrai's lunar counterpart, the Legendary Pokémon Cresselia.

Shaymin saw everyone calling Mew adorable and said 'hold my drink'. This shy cutiepie avoids interacting with others by disguising itself as a flower, and its petals are capable of absorbing toxins and pollution.

Manaphy is an unusual Mythical Pokémon, not just because it's inspired by the colorful slugs known as sea angels, but also because it's capable of breeding. Because its gender is unknown, Manaphy can only breed with Ditto. When this happens, it produces a Phione!

Gen 5 Legendary Pokémon

NameImagePokédex #TypeBase Stat Total
Cobalion#638Steel/Fighting580
Terrakion#639Rock/Fighting580
Virizion#640Grass/Fighting580
Tornadus#641Flying580
Thundurus#642Electric/Flying580
Reshiram#643Dragon/Fire680
Zekrom#644Dragon/Electric680
Landorus#645Ground/Flying600
Kyurem#646Dragon/Ice660

Known as the 'Swords of Justice', the three Fighting type Legendaries Cobalion, Terrakion,and Virizion are inspired by the Three Musketeers. Which makes it a bit strange that they appeared in Generation five, and not the France-inspired region Kalos in Generation six!

Thundurus, Landorus, and Tornadus are collectively known as the 'Forces of Nature' and would be joined by a fourth member, Enamorus, a couple of generations later. These Pokémon have almost identical 'incarnate' forms, but each one also has a more animalistic 'therian' form which sets it apart and changes its stats.

Tornadus also has the honor of being the first pure Flying type Pokémon, indicating that it's not just a creature that flies, but an elemental intrinsically connected with air.

Nicknamed the 'Tao trio' by fans, Reshiram, Zekrom, and Kyurem are all prevalent mythological creatures in the Unova region. Reshiram has potentially world-ending fire powers and a serious commitment to truth, while Zekrom has potentially world-ending lightning powers and a dedication to noble ideas.

Kyurem has a strange relationship to the other pair - this extra-terrestrial Pokémon can perform an 'absofusion' with either Reshiram or Zekrom using a DNA Splicer, becoming White Kyurem or Black Kyurem respectively. The process can be undone using the DNA Splicers again, so this isn't a situation where you need to trade with a buddy to complete this part of your Pokédex.

Gen 5 Mythical Pokémon

NameImagePokédex #TypeBase Stat Total
Victini#494Psychic/Fire600
Keldeo#647Water/Fighting580
Meloetta#648Normal/Psychic or Normal/Fighting600
Genesect#649Bug/Steel600

Victini has a unique gimmick. Whereas most Legendary and Mythical Pokémon show up at the end of the Pokédex, this is the first Unovan Pokémon - with National Dex Number #000.

There's some in-game dialogue about that number letting it 'bring victory' to the holder of the 'dex, but it's not very convincing: more likely, the designers just wanted to mark it out as special.

Keldeo is actually the adopted ward of the three Swords of Justice, who took the poor 'lil pony in after a fire separated it from its parents. That's the saddest backstory we've heard since the days of Cubone.

Meloetta actually has two formes, Aria forme - a Normal / Psychic type Pokémon - and Pirhouette forme, which is Normal / Fighting type. Aria forme is how you will first encounter Meloetta, and it needs to learn the unique move Relic Song before it can transform for the duration of a battle.

Genesect is a man-made Mythical Pokémon. A sort of robot counterpart to Mewtwo, it was resurrected from a fossil and then modified by the evil Team Plasma. Genesect's signature move Techno Blast changes type depending on the item you give to this Pokémon.

Gen 6 Legendary Pokémon

NameImagePokédex #TypeBase Stat Total
Xerneas#716Fairy680
Yveltal#717Dark/Flying680
Zygarde#718Dragon/Ground600

These three Legendary Pokémon are known as the Aura Trio by fans. They obviously resemble the letters X, Y, and Z, but are often theorized to be inspired by creatures from Celtic or Norse mythology as well, with Zygarde in particular being linked to the World Serpent Jormungandr.

Zygarde's appearance changed considerably between its first appearance in Gen 6 and its return in Gen 7.  On its first appearance, it had only its scaly, slithery appearance - but when it returned it had three 'Formes'.

See, Zygarde is actually composed of multiple components: the sentient Zygarde Cores that control its behavior, and the non-sentient Zygarde Cells that make up its body. Depending on how many of these are gathered together, it can appear as a hound-like 10% Forme, the serpentine 50% Forme, and a Power-Rangers-style Complete Forme.

Xerneas' form transformation is much less dramatic. This deerlike Pokémon spends most of its time in Normal mode, and when it transforms into Active mode its antlers and the go-faster stripes on its legs glow. In this mode it has the power to bestow eternal life, but it also looks like a Christmas decoration.

Xerneas is tasked with overseeing the balance between life and death along with its counterpart Yveltal, the physical embodiment of death and destruction. This Pokémon absorbs the life of other creatures to survive, which is very metal, but we think this is one we'd deposit in the Pokébank and leave there.

Gen 6 Mythical Pokémon

NameImagePokédex #TypeBase Stat Total
Diancie#719Rock/Fairy600
Hoopa#720Psychic/Ghost600
Volcanion#721Fire/Water600

The Mythical Pokémon Volcanion was the first Fire and Water type ever created, and three generations later, it's still the only one in the game. Which is a shame, as it's a pretty sweet type combo, with three 4x resistances.

In fact, all three of Gen 6's Mythicals broke new ground in terms of typing. Diancie is a very rare Rock / Fairy type, a status it shares with Carbink - technically it's a mutation of that much less rare 'mon. Then Hoopa is the first Psychic / Ghost type.

Gen 7 Legendary Pokémon

NameImagePokédex #TypeBase Stat Total
Type: Null#772Normal534
Silvally#773Normal570
Tapu Koko#785Electric/Fairy570
Tapu Lele#786Psychic/Fairy570
Tapu Bulu#787Grass/Fairy570
Tapu Fini#788Water/Fairy570
Cosmog#789Psychic200
Cosmoem#790Psychic400
Solgaleo#791Psychic/Steel680
Lunala#792Psychic/Ghost680

The four Tapu Pokémon - Tapu Koko, Tapu Lele, Tapu Bulu, and Tapu Fini - are guardian deities of the four islands that make up the Alola region. While most Legendary Pokémon are pretty loose in their ties to real-world mythology or religion, these four are quite clearly inspired by the four great gods of Hawaiian religion. Each has a 'shell' it can close up to form a stylized animal head.

Cosmog is a very unusual Legendary Pokémon, as it has an evolutionary line. First it becomes the massive Cosmoem, which is tied with Celesteela as the heaviest Pokémon, weighing in at a chunky 999.9kg. In the anime, Ash Ketchum carries the colossal weight around effortlessly, so I guess we can add super-strength to the boy's list of superpowers, right next to 'never ageing'.

Cosmoem can then evolve into two different Legendaries, Solgaleo and Lunala, which are conspicuously styled after the sun and moon respectively.

Cosmog's stablemate Type: Null is another evolving Legendary Pokémon, thought its line is considerably shorter - it caps out once it evolves into Silvally. It's a chimera created from cells from every known Pokémon, and was intended to fight against the dimension-leaping Ultra Beasts.

Gen 7 Mythical Pokémon

NameImagePokédex #TypeBase Stat Total
Magearna#801Steel/Fairy600
Marshadow#802Fighting/Ghost600
Zeraora#807Electric600
Meltan#808Steel300
Melmetal#809Steel600

Generation 7 really went overboard with the Mythical Pokémon, with a whopping five of them in total! And some have multiple forms they can take.

For instance, the clockwork Magearna has a basic silver form, and a painted Original Color variant with gold metallics and a red and white dress designed to look like a Pokéball. This aesthetic is also reflected in the Pokémon's Mega Evolution form, which turbo-charges its special attack.

Marshadow stands out thanks to its awesome Ghost/Fighting typing, and its spooky, shadowy appearance. Unusually, this Pokémon's shiny looks completely identical to the regular version. The difference is only noticeable when it enters its Zenith form, which activates on certain attacks. Like Magearna, the different is purely an aesthetic one, and doesn't have any gameplay effect - but it does make it a nightmare for shiny hunters to catch!

Zeraora is actually the first Mythical Pokémon with the Electric type. Impressive to be a first so late in this game's life! In Pokémon Legends Z to A's Mega Dimension DLC, this Pokémon received a new Mega form which gives it a snazzy black and blue coloration, and the highest attack stat of any electric type. It's also the fastest Mega Evolution!

Meltan and Melmetal are Mythical Pokémon that made their first appearance in the app Pokémon GO, which is still just about the only way to get them - though they can be imported to the console games Let's Go Pikachu and Let's Go Eevee via the GO Park, and Pokémon Sword and Shield via Pokémon Home.

Gen 8 Legendary Pokémon

NameImagePokédex #TypeBase Stat Total
Zacian#888Fairy670/
720
Zamazenta#889Fighting670/
720
Eternatus#890Poison/Dragon690
Kubfu#891Fighting385
Urshifu#892Fighting/Dark or Fighting/Water550
Regieleki#894Electric580
Regidrago#895Dragon580
Glastrier#896Ice580
Spectrier#897Ghost580
Calyrex#898Psychic/Grass500
Enamorus#899Fairy/Flying580

Zacian and Zamazenta are best known in their Crowned Shield/Sword forms, which they transform into when given special items to hold. They then gain an additional Steel typing, as well as a sizeable stat boost.

Not counting Dynamax and Gigantamax Pokémon, Eternatus is the tallest known Pokémon. It's actually the source of the Dynamax phenomenon that causes Pokémon to temporarily turn gigantic in the Galar region in Pokémon Sword and Shield.

On the smaller side is Kubfu, an adorable 'lil martial arts bear that evolves into one of two different types of Urshifu (Fighting/Water or Fighting/Dark) depending on where and how you train it.

Regieleki and Regidrago are two of the golem Pokémon created by the legendary Regigigas. Both were once worshiped by humans, but the cult that worshipped them eventually sought to contain and seal away the powerful creatures instead.

Glastrier and Spectrier are two proud and rather cruel horse-like Pokémon that, were it not for Calyrex, would still be terrorizing the Galar region. Despite presenting them as quite menacing, Pokédexes everywhere are keen to point out that the horses also love a good snack.

Lastly there's Enamorus, who might sound like it's eligible to be in the 'largest Pokémon' club, but their name is instead tied to themes of renewed love - fitting for a supposed god of Springtime.

Gen 8 Mythical Pokémon

NameImagePokédex #TypeBase Stat Total
Zarude#893Dark/Grass600

Zarude was added to Pokémon Sword and Shield in the Isle of Armor DLC. It has a unique move, Jungle Healing, which restores health and removes status conditions for all your Pokemon in battle, making Zarude great for double battles.

Gen 9 Legendary Pokémon

NameImagePokédex #TypeBase Stat Total
Wo-Chien#1001Dark/Grass570
Chien-Pao#1002Dark/Ice570
Ting-Lu#1003Dark/Ground570
Chi-Yu#1004Dark/Fire570
Koraidon#1007Fighting/Dragon670
Miraidon#1008Electric/Dragon670
Okidogi#1014Poison/Fighting555
Munkidori#1015Poison/Psychic555
Fezandipiti#1016Poison/Fairy555
Ogerpon#1017Grass550
Terapagos#1024Normal450/
600/
700

The core Pokémon Scarlet and Violet games added six new Legendary Pokemon Pokémon.

Wo-Chien, Chien-Pao, Ting-Lu, and Chi-Yu are known as the Calamity Pokémon. These badass Legendaries are actually cursed artifacts that absorded negative human emotions, came to life and formed bodies for themselves.

Koraidon, and Miraidon, meanwhile represent the past and future respectively. Dependent on game version, one of the two joins the player early on in Scarlet & Violet, becoming a Pokémon motorbike you can ride. We're not sure why they're needed in a world where both horse Pokémon and actual motor-vehicles exist, but they are very cool.

More Legendary Pokémon were added later in September 2023's Teal Mask DLC, forming the main storyline of that expansion's Kitakami region. These were Ogerpon - which can swap between four forms depending on the mask it's wearing - and its opposing numbers Okidogi, Munkidori, and Fezandipiti, the so-called Loyal Three.

Terapagos was added in the December 2023 Indigo Disk DLC. It's the  Legendary responsible for the 'Terastal phenomenon', which causes Pokémon to take on various new, jewel-like forms which alter their usual types.

Gen 9 Mythical Pokémon

NameImagePokédex #TypeBase Stat Total
Pecharunt#1025Poison/Ghost600

Pecharunt was added to Pokémon Scarlet and Violet in The Hidden Treasure of Area Zero Epilogue: Mochi Mayhem DLC, released in January 2024.

Unlike most Mythical Pokemon, which can easily be obtained via Mystery Gift, Pecharunt's event involved actual PLOT. You had to battle your way through trainers which Pecharunt had possessed with poisoned mochi, in order to eventually catch it.

Gen 10 Legendary Pokémon

Sorry trainers, the Legendary Pokémon of Generation 10 haven't been announced yet. You can find some rather dubious looking leaks and rumors online, but there's nothing concrete to show.

We can be sure that Pokémon Winds and Pokémon Waves will have legendary and mythical Pokémon though, presumably with one powerful beast representing the power of the skies and another embodying the seas. Perhaps it'll just be Kyogre and Rayquaza in false beards.

Fans are frankly unhealthily obsessed with this screenshot from the recent trailer. Is that suspiciously dark blob on the right the outline of a Legendary Pokémon? Or is it just a cloud? What if it's a cloud Pokémon?

Legendary Pokémon FAQ

How many Legendary Pokémon are there in total?

There are currently 71 Legendary Pokémon and 23 Mythical Pokémon.

What are Legendary Pokémon?

While there's no 'official' definition in Pokémon lore as to what exactly makes a Pokémon legendary, the general idea is that they're unique species (only one individual of each Legendary Pokémon exists) and are unusually powerful, although their power is often hidden, situational, or subtle in nature.

Legendaries often have some inherent, mystical connection to an aspect of the Pokémon world, in the manner of an animistic nature spirit, or the guardian deity of a human settlement or region.

In terms of game mechanics, they're usually non-evolving (single stage) Pokémon with unusually high in-game stats in one area or another, and they're usually genderless - although, as you read the rest of this section, you'll find that's not always true.

What seems to unite all Legendary Pokémon is that people in the Pokémon world tell stories about them, for one reason or another; they have a legend. Hence the name.

What's the difference between Legendary and Mythical Pokémon?

Legendary Pokémon are incredibly rare, but Mythical Pokémon are so rare that people in the Pokémon world doubt their very existence. In gameplay terms, there is one version of every Legendary Pokémon available in their respective games, but Mythical Pokémon were originally only obtainable during exclusive events. If you weren't around while they were being given away, there was no way to access them.

However, by now most Mythical Pokémon have either appeared in mainline games, or become accessible through other means, like completing a Pokédex on Pokémon HOME. Not all of them, though, Zarude and Victini are the only two Mythicals that have never been released outside of limited-time events.

Does Pokémon Legends Z-A add new Legendary Pokémon?

No, Pokémon Legends Z-A doesn't introduce any completely new Legendary Pokémon species to the setting.

However, the game does include a brand new Mega Evolution form for one existing legendary: you can catch Zygarde in this game and evolve it into Mega Zygarde with a Zygardite Stone. Though the Legendary Pokémon shows up in the story much earlier, you can't trap it in your balls until the post-game. The tutorial below shows how:

The Mega Dimension DLC added three more mega-evolved legendaries: Mega Darkrai, Mega Heatran, and Mega Zeraora, with Mega Darkrai being pretty core to the story.

What is the strongest Legendary Pokémon?

All the Legendary Pokémon are pretty powerful, but in terms of pure raw stats, Arceus is the strongest. With 120 in every single statistic, Arceus has a base stat total of 720.

That said, other Legendary Pokémon have various forms that can match or even surpass the god of the Pokémon universe. Zacian and Zamazenta can match it in their Crowned Sword and Crowned Shield forms, for instance, and Terapagos comes close, with 700 stats in its Stellar Form.

But Mega Rayquaza and both forms of Mega Mewtwo are even stronger than Arceus, with combined stats totalling 780.

These are the most powerful Legendary Pokémon that a player can harness in-game, but even they are dwarfed by Eternamax Eternatus, which has a ridiculous stat total of 1,125. This is purely a boss fight however; the player cannot harness this legendary power themselves.

What's the weakest Legendary Pokémon?

Fans generally agree that Cosmog is the weakest Legendary Pokémon in the videogames. Its basic stats are pitiful and it can only learn two moves: Teleport (which switches it out of the battle) and Splash (which explicitly doesn't do anything).

Like Magikarp, its raison d'être is purely to evolve into stronger forms. In Cosmog's case, that's Cosmoem, followed by one of the twin Gen 7 Legendaries, Solgaleo and Lunala.

In the Pokémon TCG, Cosmog has a little more going for it. Some Cosmog cards allow you to draw cards and prevent damage to it while it's on your Bench. Ultimately, though, it's still a pitiable weakling that's only there to evolve into more powerful 'Mons.

What's the rarest Legendary Pokémon?

In the world of Pokémon, all the Legendary Pokémon are equally rare: there's just one of each of them. The Mythical Pokémon aren't rarer, they're just much less widely known about, and generally sighted more rarely by people in the world of Pokémon.

In our world, the rarest Legendary Pokémon from the videogames is most likely Diancie. The last time you could get a Diancie was at a 2016 South Korean real-world event, as a gift for Omega Ruby or Alpha Sapphire.

If we're talking Pokémon TCG, the rarest Legendary card, by value, is First Edition Neo Genesis Holo Lugia, from the year 2000. Experts reckon there are only 41 copies in the world that are graded at the PSA 10 'pristine' level - and one sold at auction in 2021 for a terrifying $114,300.

Do Legendary Pokémon come in groups?

Many Legendary Pokémon are members of a group, usually introduced to the setting at the same time, as part of the same generation of Pokémon. Examples of these groups include the original Gen 1  Legendary Birds, a trio of Articuno, Moltres, and Zapdos, and Gen 7's 'Legendary quartet' of Tapu Bulu, Tapu Fini, Tapu Koko, and Tapu Lele - known as the Guardian Deities.

With some exceptions - like the Lunar Duo of Darkrai and Cresselia - Mythical Pokémon are not organized into groups, but stand alone as their own entities.

Who was the first Legendary Pokémon to exist?

The first Legendary Pokémon to exist in the Pokémon world was either Arceus or Mew - but there's no way to be sure which, and fan theories abound on either side.

Arceus, the 'god' of Pokémon, is said via in-game descriptions to have created the universe and every Pokémon in it; but Poké-scientists also believe Mew to be the 'ancestor' of all the other species.

Some fans theorize that they created each other in the time before time existed in the Pokémon universe - i.e. before Arceus created Dialga, the godlike Legendary Pokémon with power over time. But ultimately which came first - Arceus or Mew - will likely always remain a mystery.

Which Legendary Pokémon does Ash have?

Famously, Ash Ketchum, hero of the original Pokémon anime, has never actually caught a Legendary Pokémon - though he has bonded and allied with several in his journeys, using his apparently supernatural levels of lovable charisma, most notably a Cosmoem (later evolving into Solgaleo) which he nicknames 'Nebby'.

Ash does catch one Mythical Pokémon - Meltan - during the Sun & Moon series, which later evolves into Ash's Melmetal and has stayed with him ever since.

Is Arceus really a god?

To all intents and purposes, Arceus is a god within the Pokémon world. In Pokémon canon, Arceus is believed to have created the universe and all other Pokémon - which implies that it also created the humans that call this universe their home.

Your philosophical definitions of 'god' may vary, but in our books, a pre-existing, ultra-powerful entity that created the universe and at least some of the living things in it qualifies as one.

Can Legendary Pokémon evolve?

Yes, some Legendary Pokémon can evolve - but most can't, and the ones that can sometimes do it in unusual ways, compared to regular Pokémon.

Gen 6's Type: Null (evolving into Silvally) and Cosmog (evolving into Cosmoem) were the first to have regular evolutions, with Cosmoem going on to evolve into either Solgaleo, in Pokémon Sun, or Lunala in Pokémon Moon.

There are several Mythical and Legendary Pokémon that have Mega Evolutions: Rayquaza, Mewtwo (which has an X and Y form), Latias, Latios, and Diancie.

Kyogre and Groudon also have 'Primal Reversions' introduce in Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire. They work a lot like Mega Evolutions, but are specific to those Pokémon.

Do Legendary Pokémon have genders?

No, most Legendary Pokémon have no gender - but there are some exceptions.

Four Legendaries can canonically only be female:

  • Cresselia
  • Enamorus
  • Latias
  • Ogerpon

Seven can only be male:

  • Fezandipiti
  • Landorus
  • Latios
  • Munkidori
  • Okidogi
  • Thundurus
  • Tornadus

And three can be male or female:

  • Heatran
  • Kubfu
  • Urshifu

Is Mew a boy or a girl?

Like most Legendary and Mythical Pokémon, Mew has no gender. Mew is a perfect, faultless, innocent interdimensional baby and must be protected at all costs. Mew shows us a state of existence as it could be, untroubled by mortal concerns like the social construct of gender, at one with past, present, and future. Be like Mew.

Why does Mewtwo hate Mew?

In the original 2000 Pokémon movie, Mewtwo hates Mew because of jealousy, because Mew is the 'original' Pokémon and Mewtwo believes itself to be an imperfect clone.

However, after a dramatic battle with Ash Ketchum at the climax of the first movie, Mewtwo experiences a major change of heart, softening his hatred of humans and shifting his burning resentment for Mew into a place of understanding.

In the Mewtwo Returns TV series, first aired in the US in 2001, Mewtwo's character becomes more nuanced and even heroic at times, with the once murderous Legendary 'mon rescuing both humans and Pokémon, and aiming to avoid combat at all costs.

Who is stronger, Mew or Mewtwo?

When Mew and Mewtwo face off in Pokémon: The First Movie, the fight ends inconclusively. All the Pokémon are horrified by the (temporary) death of Ash Ketchum, and the battle stops.

In the Pokémon games, the answer is simple - Mewtwo wipes the floor with Mew. It just has much more powerful stats. Mew, like many Mythical Pokémon, has 100 in every base stat. With 130 Speed and 154 Special Attack, Mewtwo gets to act first and deals way more damage.

Does Mew evolve into Mewtwo?

Mew does not evolve into Mewtwo. Mewtwo is a cloned Pokèmon made using samples of Mew's DNA: they're related, but not necessarily the same species.

Are there Legendary Pokémon cards?

Yes, Legendary Pokémon from every generation appear in a whole variety of cards for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. The more popular Legendary or Mythical 'mons often get picked for the fancier foil and illustration card treatments saved for the rarest printed cards, meaning they can end up being the most desirable to collect.

However, it's important to remember that that's not a rule in the TCG. Legendary and Mythical Pokémon have appeared on cards of all rarities, including standard common cards.

What are Pokémon LEGEND cards?

Briefly, during the HeartGold & SoulSilver card sets of the early 2010s, the Pokémon TCG introduced a small set of variant cards which exclusively featured Legendary Pokémon - their most distinctive aspect being that each 'card' was in fact two regular sized cards, which created a combined artwork when laid edge to edge.

Of the nine such two-card combos released, seven featured a pair of Legendaries together (one on each half). The other two are the two Gen 2 Legendary birds Ho-Oh and Lugia - with the wild-looking, two-part Lugia LEGEND now one of the most valuable Lugia cards.

Wargamer regularly tracks down deals on Pokémon packs, and you can stay informed by joining our friendly Discord community.

title: Mega Empires might be the world's largest board game, but it still respects your time
content:
When it comes to the world's biggest board game, there are many pretenders to the throne. The infamous Campaign for North Africa boasts the longest playtime, while World in Flames won a Guiness World Record for its square footage. Hell, there are a dozen roll-and-writes that promise player counts in the hundreds. What makes Mega Empires special? Is it really, as its website claims, the biggest board game in the world?

Co-designer Flo de Haan admits to me that 'biggest board game in the world' is "a bit of a marketing term". But there's merit there, too, because Mega Empires has everything you'd expect from a game with 'mega' in its title. "The length of the game, the number of components, the number of players, the size of the board - with all these things combined", de Haan says, "there's no bigger game than that".

Mega Empires first released in 2022 as a remaster of 2015's Mega Civilization. It's a civ-building strategy board game that emulates the real-world growth (and decline) of empires throughout history. Mega Empires is technically four board games, each standalone yet compatible.

The West and The East expansions cover the Mediterranean Sea, North Africa, and the Arabian Peninsula and Southwest Asia. Those two boxes alone accommodate three to 19 players. Then, there's The Far East - North and The Far East - South. Mapping out East Asia, these two expansions arrive in 2027, and they bring the player count up to 30 people.

A full game of Mega Empires now involves a board that's almost nine feet long. That doesn't include the many player mats, tracking boards, and cards involved. I can't verify whether Mega Empires breaks the world record set by World in Flames - but I can verify this game is freakin' huge.

What makes Mega Empires stand out from other monster board games is its approachability. "We wanted it to play very simply", de Haan tells me. "It's really easy to learn, but the options are enormous." "

As with almost any strategy game, your aim is to score the most victory points. You lead an asymmetric empire, and you mark your advancements by climbing the Archaeological Success Tracker (AST). You also score based on the value of your Civilization Advances, combined with the number of cities you maintain.

Cities produce commodities, which you can use to pay for powerful Civilization Advances, or to trade with other players. Trading also allows you to sneak Calamities into their hands - which can topple a civilization if not properly managed.

It's a careful mix of area control, economic management, bluffing and diplomacy. The two Far East expansions are aimed at small player groups of three to five players, but even with the full 30, a game still plays over 15 rounds. That's a mere 12 hours! A long time by the standards of a casual gamer, but a pittance compared to games like Campaign for North Africa.

"We always intended it to be a long game", de Haan says, "but it was designed to fit in one day. You can start at nine in the morning, then play until nine in the evening, ready for people to catch trains home."

In fact, Mega Empires might be the perfect game after you first get into the hobby. Seriously, hear me out.

"Mega Empires is actually Catan for advanced players", de Haan says. "It's the next step up. You build cities, and you connect them on a board, and you trade with people." That's quite the simplification of Mega Empires' rules, but the core tenets are certainly Catan-esque.

The major difference, de Haan says, isn't complexity - it's ideology. "In Catan, you build up to a final point where you have X cities or points, and then you win the game", he explains. "But there's an expansion where you have to contend with Barbarians who destroy your cities and roads. Meg Empires shares this idea, because you have to understand you will lose the things you build."

As the Kickstarter for the Far East expansions put it, Mega Empires is "a cycle of constant destruction and recovery". "During a round you build up a little, but also your cities will be destroyed, and you have to build up again", de Haan says. You have to be vigilant for Calamities, trading at the right time or finding spots to rebuild your cities."

That non-linear progression might irk the hardcore eurogame fan, but it's a more authentic mapping of real-world history. And history is very important to mechanics of Mega Empires.

Take, for example, the new expansions arriving in 2027. According to de Haan, the Far East expansions replace the floodplains of West and East with rivers, because historically "Chinese and Tibetan rivers are really impactful".

"You can move your tokens two steps instead of one when using a river downstream", he tells me. "But the Song Dynasty invented the pound lock, so this is also an Advance". "If you have the pound lock, you can also move two steps upstream on the river." Other Advances reflect the inventions of East Asian inventions from 200 AD to the year 1200: the magnetic compass, gunpowder, and more. The game's new components consider the impact of paper, silk, and Mongolian Horsemanship.

As for other historically accurate mechanics, "we have fully integrated pirate ships, and these block sea movement unless you pay them a tribute card". "If you do, you can also move them to your neighbor and place barbarian tokens to attack someone's city."

Plus, "We added Zodiac events to the AST". "When the turn market hits a token, it triggers a random event - mostly a Calamity for all players, but sometimes they only hit players who are in the lead, or benefit those falling behind." "It's a real balancer", de Haan adds.

There's even a Great Wall card that adds physical barriers to the board, impassable unless you also have a Great Wall card - or gunpowder to bring the whole thing down.

The Far East expansions fine-tune the Mega Empires experience in many ways, at both ends of the player count spectrum. Cultural Heritage cards kickstart a smaller game (and there's even some designed for the existing West and East modules). Meanwhile, trading has expanded via The Silk Road, not just to accommodate higher player counts, but to reflect the impact of trade on the region.

I asked de Haan if he could see Mega Empires getting any bigger. After all, there's still a lot of world left to cover. He says he and the team can see them designing more modules, but the player count is likely to stick at 30. "We considered it during design, and we said 'okay, this is the limit'", he tells me. "Another player won't add anything more."

"In future, we'd really like to design other Mega Empires games", he says. "Perhaps in other parts of the world, or other timespans, or focusing on specific regions - but we will not add more players to this world."

You can check out demos of Far East: North and Far East: South at this year's Essen Spiel, or when they see a full release in 2027. Until then, if you want to learn more about the year's best board games, check out our dedicated guide - or hit us up in the Wargamer Discord.
